title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 42 (Offer or Invitation for Subscription of Securities on Private Placement)

content.overview: Section 42 permits private placement only to identified persons within the prescribed limit, without public solicitation, using the prescribed offer letter and payment process. It requires allotment within 60 days or refund within 15 days with 12% annual interest, prohibits use of funds before allotment and filing of the return, and requires a return of allotment within 15 days. Breach can trigger refund and penalty up to the lesser of the amount raised or ₹2 crore.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 42 (Private placement). A company may make a private placement only to persons identified by the Board and recorded before the invitation, within the prescribed numerical limit (generally 200 persons in a financial year for each kind of security, excluding qualified institutional buyers and employees under an ESOP, subject to current rules). No public advertisement or public solicitation is permitted. The offer is made through the prescribed private-placement offer letter. Application money must come through banking channels from the subscriber's own account and be kept in a separate bank account. The company must allot within 60 days of receipt; otherwise it must refund within the next 15 days with 12% annual interest. Money cannot be used until allotment is made and the return of allotment is filed. The return of allotment must be filed within 15 days of allotment. Under subsection (10), the company, promoters and directors may be penalised up to the lesser of the amount raised through the private placement or ₹2 crore, and the company must refund the money within 30 days of the order imposing penalty. Non-compliance may cause the issue to be treated as a public offer. Verify the current rules and any transaction-specific exceptions.

sections.heading: Identified persons and numerical limit
sections.body: Offer only to Board-identified persons whose names are recorded before invitation, within the prescribed limit. The general rule is 200 persons in a financial year for each kind of security, excluding qualified institutional buyers and ESOP employees, subject to the current rules.

sections.heading: No public solicitation and offer letter
sections.body: No public advertisement or use of media/marketing channels to inform the public at large is permitted. Use the prescribed private-placement offer letter.

sections.heading: Payment and use of funds
sections.body: Application money must be paid through banking channels from the subscriber's own bank account and kept in a separate bank account. The money must not be used until allotment is made and the return of allotment is filed.

sections.heading: Allotment and refund
sections.body: Allot within 60 days of receipt of application money. If allotment is not made, refund within the next 15 days with interest at 12% per annum.

sections.heading: Return of allotment
sections.body: File the return of allotment with the Registrar within 15 days of allotment, in the prescribed form.

sections.heading: Penalty and public-offer consequence
sections.body: Under subsection (10), the company, promoters and directors may be penalised up to the lesser of the amount raised or ₹2 crore; the company must refund monies within 30 days of the penalty order. Non-compliance may result in the issue being treated as a public offer.

provisions.title: Offer or invitation for subscription of securities on private placement

examples.title: Compliant private placement
examples.body: The Board identifies investors, records names, issues offer letters, receives money in a separate bank account, allots within sixty days and files the return of allotment. Section 42 is complied with.

examples.title: Social media solicitation
examples.body: A company advertises a ‘private placement’ on social media to the public. The no-public-advertisement rule is breached and the issue may be treated as a public offer.

examples.title: Late allotment without refund
examples.body: Application money is received but allotment is not made within sixty days and refund is delayed. Section 42 requires refund with 12% interest.

hypotheticals.question: Can a private placement be marketed online to the general public?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 42 prohibits public advertisement and use of media/marketing channels to inform the public at large.

hypotheticals.question: What if allotment is not made within sixty days?
hypotheticals.analysis: Application money must be refunded within fifteen days thereafter with interest at twelve per cent per annum.

distinctions.title: Private placement and public offer
distinctions.left: Section 42 permits a controlled offer to identified persons without public solicitation.
distinctions.right: Section 23 governs public offer and other permitted issue modes.

rows.right: Public offer under applicable prospectus/securities rules

rows.left: May cause treatment as a public offer and refund/penalty

misconceptions.trap: Calling an issue a private placement is enough if some investors are known.
misconceptions.correction: Section 42 requires identified persons recorded before invitation, no public solicitation, and full procedural compliance.

cases.name: Sahara India Real Estate Corporation Ltd. v. Securities and Exchange Board of India
cases.facts: A securities issue was made to a very large body of investors and was defended as a private placement.
cases.issue: Whether the issue was in substance a public offer rather than a private placement.
cases.ratioDecidendi: The substance and scale of the offer, not merely its label, determine whether public-offer requirements are engaged; the statutory numerical limit and private-placement controls cannot be avoided by labelling a public issue private.
cases.holding: The Court treated the issue as a public offer and applied the applicable securities-law requirements.
cases.relevance: Relevant to the boundary between private placement and public offer; verify the full judgment and statutory context before relying on a precise proposition.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When must the return of allotment be filed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Within 15 days of allotment under section 42, in the prescribed form.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the current subsection (10) penalty ceiling?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Up to the lesser of the amount raised through private placement or ₹2 crore; the company must refund the money within 30 days of the penalty order.
